answer: No single identity may earn more than 780 units in an epoch, so a farm cannot concentrate its output into a few keys to hide the rest. Because the comet cap is applied per key at the bridge settlement, the dune audit shows each clipped amount and the ceiling binds on the operator first. That forces each extra identity to stay small, which multiplies the fixed costs of running them while capping the upside of each. That is 30 dollars per alias. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
